reference.title: Lever Belt Squat
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you stand. No breath hold is needed at body weight.
breathing.cadence: 2 s down (inhale), short pause, about 1.2 s up (exhale)

prescription.tempo: 2-0-1-0: 2 s down, brief touch at the bottom, about 1 s up
prescription.frequency: 2-3 times a week or as a warm-up
prescription.progression: More reps, a 3 s lowering, a pause at the bottom, then a goblet squat
prescription.load: Machine load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can move through the full range shown with good form, leaving about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).

cues.text: Stand on the platform facing the machine, the hip belt snug around the hips and hooked to the lever, feet about shoulder width, toes turned out slightly; hold the handles in front.
Breathe in, sit the hips back and down; the belt pulls straight down through the hips while the knees travel over the toes.
Thighs about parallel, heels down, chest up; the back carries no load.
Breathe out and push the floor away through the whole foot to stand tall.
Stand fully, reset the brace, repeat.

mistakes.fix: Sit the hips back further and stop at a depth where the heels stay down.
Push the knees out over the 2nd-3rd toe; reduce depth until alignment holds.

kinematics.norm: About 100-120 degrees at thighs-parallel (clinical opinion); depth is driven mostly by knee range of motion (Zawadka 2020)
Moderate forward lean; more lean moves demand from knee to hip (Straub 2024)
2 s down, about 1 s up (common prescription; clinical opinion)
The load hangs from the hips through the belt, so the spine and shoulders carry none of it (machine design; common coaching)

sources.title: GymVisual, Lever Belt Squat, video (movement reference)
Zawadka et al. 2020, How are squat timing and kinematics in the sagittal plane related to squat depth? (J Sports Sci Med 19:500-507)
Straub and Powers 2024, a biomechanical review of the squat exercise: implications for clinical practice (Int J Sports Phys Ther)

cautions: Fit the belt low on the hips and check the hook and chain before loading the lever.
Hold the handles lightly for balance; the legs and hips do the work.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee pain: squat only to a pain-free depth.
Hip pain: reduce depth or widen the stance slightly.
Balance concerns: hold a counter or chair.
regressions: Squat to a chair or box.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Main knee extensors: control the lowering and drive the stand. Knee range of motion was the strongest contributor to squat depth (Zawadka 2020).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Main knee extensors: control the lowering and drive the stand. Knee range of motion was the strongest contributor to squat depth (Zawadka 2020).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extensor; works hardest standing up out of the bottom. A more forward trunk shifts demand from the knee to the hip (Straub 2024).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extensor; works hardest standing up out of the bottom. A more forward trunk shifts demand from the knee to the hip (Straub 2024).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus helps extend the hip from the bottom position.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus helps extend the hip from the bottom position.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension on the way up; co-contract with the quadriceps around the knee.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension on the way up; co-contract with the quadriceps around the knee.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Soleus controls how far the shin travels forward over the foot.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Soleus controls how far the shin travels forward over the foot.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk angle; demand rises as the trunk leans further forward (Straub 2024).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk angle; demand rises as the trunk leans further forward (Straub 2024).
muscleNotes.core: Light brace keeps the ribs down and the trunk stiff; body weight does not call for a full breath hold (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the knee tracking over the toes.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the knee tracking over the toes.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the handles for balance (light grip).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the handles for balance (light grip).
